papers.title: Lactobacillus-Based Therapy for Ulcerative Colitis: From Strain Heterogeneity and TCM-Mediated Modulation to Engineered Delivery and Precision Translation.
papers.authors: Zhang T, Lei H, Zhao X, Wang H, Chen X, Zhai Y et al.
papers.abstract: Although Lactobacillus sensu lato is widely considered a promising microecological intervention for ulcerative colitis, its clinical translation remains severely constrained by strain-specific efficacy, host microenvironmental dependency, and the risk of opportunistic systemic translocation across a compromised intestinal barrier. The historical assumption of genus-level therapeutic uniformity is increasingly inadequate, as even closely related strains can exhibit divergent or occasionally adverse clinical outcomes. This functional heterogeneity is rooted in distinct genomic architectures encoding carbohydrate-active enzymes, bile salt hydrolases, and surface adhesins, which collectively govern the metabolic and colonization behavior of live biotherapeutics. Furthermore, selectively expanding target strains within a competitive, exclusionary gut microbiota represents a major clinical bottleneck. To address these barriers, this review synthesizes the common protective networks of lactobacilli and the taxonomic heterogeneity that defines their efficacy and safety boundaries. We review how traditional Chinese medicine constituents may selectively modulate target strains through the potential substrate-enzyme compatibility and summarize advanced bioengineering platforms, including postbiotics (inactivated-cell preparations) and cell-free effector components, and responsive biomaterials, designed to protect these metabolic pathways. By deconstructing the molecular logic of functional divergence and pharmacological targeting, we argue that a promising direction for precision microecological therapy may involve moving beyond broad taxonomic classification toward quantitative matching of strain-specific functional and enzymatic fingerprints. This paradigm shift demands rigorous causal validation, context-responsive delivery systems, and a regulatory transition toward quality control standards incorporating biochemical effector activity units alongside, rather than instead of, viable-cell enumeration.

papers.title: Chinese herbal medicine formulas for Alzheimer's disease: Evidence, mechanisms, and translational standards.
papers.authors: Liang EX, Li QW, Liang H
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is defined biologically by amyloid and tau pathology. The emergence of biomarker-based diagnostic criteria, blood-based assays, and anti-amyloid therapeutic trials has substantially raised the evidentiary standard for all candidate AD interventions, including Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) formulas. However, CHM formula evidence for AD lacks critical appraisal and methodological standards. Thus, this review aims to: (1) critically evaluate the clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence for oral or topical CHM formulas used in AD, specifically those selected according to Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnostic; and (2) assess the methodological requirements necessary for credible development of such formulas in AD research. Preclinical studies suggest plausible effects of CHM formulas on amyloid-related pathways, tau phosphorylation, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and energy metabolism, but these findings remain hypothesis-generating rather than clinically validated. Most included studies relied on clinical diagnoses, likely encompassing mixed pathologies (e.g., vascular dementia, dementia with Lewy bodies, or depression-related cognitive impairment), rendering their results preliminary rather than confirmatory for biologically defined AD. Current evidence does not support CHM formulas as established therapies for AD. Future studies will require biomarker-confirmed diagnosis, rigorous formula quality control, prespecified TCM pattern stratification, clinically meaningful cognitive and functional endpoints, mechanistic target-engagement measures, and prospective safety and herb-drug interaction monitoring.

papers.title: SPIRIT-A: An Extension of SPIRIT 2025 for Acupuncture Clinical Trial Protocols.
papers.authors: Duan Y, Lin H, Zhou Z, Lee MS, Alraek T, Chan AW et al.
papers.abstract:
Protocols for acupuncture randomized controlled trials (RCTs) often lack adequate reporting of acupuncture-specific features. This study developed the Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials-Acupuncture (SPIRIT-A) extension to provide tailored reporting guidance for acupuncture clinical trial protocols.
The study followed EQUATOR Network guidance for developing health research reporting guidelines. A Development Group, Advisory Group, and international Delphi expert panel were established. The initial checklist was informed by two reviews assessing reporting quality using SPIRIT and Standard Protocol Items for Clinical Trials with Traditional Chinese Medicine (SPIRIT-TCM) extension respectively, and refined with reference to SPIRIT 2025, STandards for Reporting Interventions in Controlled Trials of Acupuncture (STRICTA), and the SPIRIT-TCM extension. A modified Delphi survey was conducted according to a predefined consensus criterion (≥80% agreement), followed by final expert endorsement.
Thirty-four experts from 10 countries participated in the Delphi survey, and all candidate items reached the predefined consensus threshold. The final checklist includes 34 items (57 subitems) that supplement SPIRIT 2025 with acupuncture-specific recommendations covering syndrome differentiation and treatment, procedural details, blinding and control design, acupuncturist qualifications, and safety monitoring.
SPIRIT-A provides structured reporting recommendations addressing key methodological considerations in acupuncture clinical trial protocols. Its development followed internationally recognized methodological standards and is expected to enhance the completeness and reproducibility of acupuncture RCT protocols and facilitate their broader dissemination and use.

papers.title: Research Progress of Astragali Complanati Semen Based on Bibliometric Analysis: Herbal Textual Research, Processing, Chemical Constituents, and Pharmacological Activities.
papers.authors: Wu H, Li D, Yang H, Li Z, Wang J, Zhao H et al.
papers.abstract:
Astragali Complanati Semen (ACS), the dried mature seeds of Astragalus complanatus R. Br., is a traditional Chinese medicine with a long history of medicinal use. According to traditional Chinese medicinal records, ACS is traditionally used for tonifying the kidney and strengthening yang, consolidating essence and reducing urinary frequency, and nourishing the liver and improving visual function. Modern phytochemical and pharmacological studies have revealed that ACS contains various bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, triterpenoid saponins, amino acids, fatty acids, sterols, sesquiterpenoids, polysaccharides, and trace elements, which may contribute to its traditional therapeutic applications.
This review aimed to identify research trends and hotspots in ACS and to summarize its geo-authenticity, processing methods, chemical constituents, pharmacological activities, mechanisms, and future prospects.
Bibliometric visualization was performed using publications retrieved from the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform (Wanfang), VIP Chinese Science and Technology Journal Database (VIP), Web of Science (WoS), and PubMed. The findings were integrated with a comprehensive review of herbal textual research, processing, chemical constituents, pharmacological effects, and mechanisms.
The number of publications increased steadily, with China accounting for the largest share. Institutions from 28 Chinese provinces and municipalities contributed, with Shaanxi Province showing the highest publication frequency. Research hotspots included geo-authenticity, processing, chemical constituents, pharmacological activities, and mechanisms. ACS contains diverse chemical constituents, including flavonoids, sesquiterpenoids, triterpenoid saponins, polysaccharides, and other constituents. Major pharmacological activities include antihypertensive, lipid-lowering, hepatoprotective, antifibrotic, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects.
This review clarifies ACS research trends and hotspots and comprehensively summarizes its major research domains. Future studies should focus on quality markers (Q-markers), the activities and mechanisms of flavonoid monomers, and the isolation, purification, structural characterization, and structure-activity relationships of polysaccharides.

papers.title: HaloTag-directed magnetic immobilization of PAD4 for target-based screening of natural-product inhibitors.
papers.authors: Xu H, Zhu D, Zhao Z, Zuo H, Wang Y, Fang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Target-directed screening of bioactive natural products is often limited by the instability, poor recoverability, and repeated preparation requirements of soluble recombinant enzymes. Here, we developed a reusable magnetic peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) screening platform based on site-directed HaloTag immobilization. Recombinant Halo-PAD4 was captured directly from crude lysate by chloroalkane-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs-Cl) without an additional labor-intensive and time-consuming enzyme purification step, generating MNPs-Halo-PAD4 with retained catalytic activity and inhibitor responsiveness. Compared with soluble PAD4, the immobilized enzyme showed improved activity retention during storage and temperature exposure and could be magnetically recovered for repeated assays. The platform was applied to screen water, 75% ethanol, and ethyl acetate extracts of 15 traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) materials. Among the tested materials, Alpinia officinarum consistently exhibited the strongest PAD4-inhibitory activity in both soluble and immobilized PAD4 assays. Activity-guided high-performance liquid chromatography fractionation localized the inhibitory activity to fraction F3. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry tentatively annotated 13 constituents, and authentic-standard testing prioritized galangin. Galangin inhibited PAD4 with an IC50 value of 46.6 μM and showed direct interaction with PAD4 by biolayer interferometry, with an apparent KD of 7.8 μM. Molecular docking further provided a structural hypothesis for the interaction. This workflow combines HaloTag-chloroalkane chemistry, magnetic enzyme immobilization, liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry for the screening of PAD4 inhibitors. This proposed one-step capture and immobilization of recombinant protein also supports ligand screening for other protein targets.

papers.title: Comparative Efficacy of Different Moxibustion Therapies on Pain and Functional Improvement in Knee Osteoarthritis: A Network Meta-Analysis.
papers.authors: Wang M, Ye Y, Cheng Y, Pan L, Chen Y
papers.abstract:
This network meta-analysis aimed to systematically compare the efficacy of various moxibustion therapies in alleviating pain, improving joint function, and increasing the overall response rate in patients with knee osteoarthritis (KOA). Additionally, this study explored potential sources of heterogeneity to provide evidence-based support for clinical decision-making.
We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and SinoMed from inception to March 30, 2026, for RCTs evaluating moxibustion modalities for KOA. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using ROB 2.0. Network meta-analysis was conducted in Stata 17.0 using a frequentist framework. Effects were expressed as SMDs or RRs with 95% CIs, and treatments were ranked by SUCRA. Heterogeneity, inconsistency, and evidence certainty were assessed using Cochran's Q test, node-splitting analysis, and CINeMA, respectively.
For pain (23 RCTs, 1,740 participants), heat-sensitive moxibustion was the only intervention significantly better than usual care (SMD -2.27, 95% CI -4.47 to -0.07; SUCRA 83.9%). For joint function (17 RCTs, 1,459 participants), heat-sensitive and conventional moxibustion were both significant, with heat-sensitive moxibustion ranking highest (SUCRA 78%). For overall response rate (8 trials, 702 participants), conventional moxibustion was superior to usual care (RR 1.35, 95% CI 1.08-1.80; SUCRA 97.3%). Certainty of evidence was low to very low.
Evidence of low to very low certainty indicates that heat-sensitive moxibustion may improve pain and joint function compared with usual care, while conventional moxibustion may increase the overall response rate. However, no moxibustion modality demonstrated clear overall superiority over others. These findings warrant cautious interpretation. Larger, multicentre RCTs with standardized protocols and robust blinding are needed to clarify comparative effectiveness.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture for Procedural Anesthesia: A Scoping Review of Stimulation Parameters and Anesthetic-Sparing Outcomes.
papers.authors: Lee C, Chu H, Kim K, Park S, Kang K, Kim S et al.
papers.abstract:
Pharmacological local anesthetics carry risks of systemic toxicity and hypersensitivity and do not attenuate the surgical stress response. Electroacupuncture (EA) has been proposed as an adjunct for procedural anesthesia, but the heterogeneous clinical evidence has not been systematically mapped.
This scoping review was registered on the Open Science Framework and follows PRISMA-ScR. PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Web of Science, CNKI and J-STAGE were searched from inception to April 8, 2026, without language restrictions. Eligible human studies used needle-based EA, alone or with pharmacological anesthesia, for procedural local or regional anesthesia, nerve block or local anesthetic dose reduction. Consistent with scoping review methodology, no formal critical appraisal or risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken.
Thirty-nine studies published between 1971 and 2025 were included: randomized controlled trials (59%), non-randomized and observational studies (36%) and case reports (5%), spanning minor soft-tissue, head and neck, anorectal and abdominal, and spinal and orthopedic procedures, mixed surgical series and experimental pain models. Of the 20 studies that quantified local anesthetic consumption, seven allowed calculation of reductions relative to controls (10%-86%), which were calculated on different dose bases and are not directly comparable. A small number of studies reported no requirement for supplemental local anesthetic or rescue medication. The dense-disperse 2/100 Hz waveform with a 20-30-minute pre-operative induction phase was the most frequently used protocol in trials published from 2012 onward.
This review maps potentially promising stimulation parameters but cannot establish the efficacy or clinical superiority of EA. The 2/100 Hz protocol with structured pre-operative induction should be regarded as a hypothesis-generating starting point for standardized trials, for which this evidence map provides a design framework. Kilohertz-frequency stimulation, studied only experimentally, is a hypothesis for future research.
Open Science Framework, DOI: https://osf.io/4n357 (registered April 28, 2026).
Clinical trial number: not applicable.

papers.title: Association of HTR3A and COMT polymorphisms with electroacupuncture response for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in breast cancer: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.authors: Zheng Y, Xiao W, Guan Y, Zhao F, Li J, Wang Z et al.
papers.abstract:
Preliminary findings indicate that electroacupuncture (EA) reduces chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV), yet individual responses vary. This study aimed to explore associations between selected single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and complete protection (CP) against CINV and to conduct an exploratory evaluation of their predictive value.
This exploratory analysis was based on a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of EA (NCT05275569). Three candidate SNPs in HTR3A and COMT were genotyped by Sanger sequencing. The primary outcome measure was CP against CINV, defined according to the endpoint of the prospective study. Firth logistic regression was applied to evaluate associations between clinical or genetic variables and CP under additive, dominant and recessive models.
A total of 189 patients with breast cancer (BC) were enrolled, with 96 allocated to true EA group and 93 to sham EA group. The two groups were comparable in clinical variables and genotype distribution, and all three SNPs conformed to Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE). In the true EA group, CP achievement rates varied by rs909411 genotype: 42.9% (AA), 32.1% (AG), and 62.3% (GG) (P = 0.027). Univariable Firth logistic regression indicated that rs909411 was associated with a higher likelihood of achieving CP under both additive (OR = 2.088, 95% CI: 1.089-4.249, P = 0.026) and recessive models (OR = 3.080, 95% CI: 1.327-7.429, P = 0.009). After Multivariable adjustment, rs909411 remained statistically significant (additive: OR = 2.138, P = 0.027; recessive: OR = 3.241, P = 0.011). rs4633 was associated with a lower likelihood of achieving CP under the recessive model (univariable OR = 0.089, P = 0.035; Multivariable OR = 0.059, P = 0.016). No consistent association was observed for rs4680, and no significant SNP-by-treatment interactions were detected.
Exploratory treatment-stratified analyses identified associations of rs909411 and rs4633 with CP within the true EA group.

papers.title: Entropy-driven DNA circuit coupled with Cas9 trans-cleavage for dual-amplified label-free electrochemical sensing of aflatoxin B1 and lead ions.
papers.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
papers.authors: Lei J, Chen F, Shi K
papers.abstract: Sensitive and reliable detection of hazardous contaminants in food and pharmaceutical products is important for public health and quality control. Herein, we developed ECG-Cas9 (Entropy-driven Circuit-assisted G-quadruplex Electrochemical Cas9 sensing) by coupling an entropy-driven DNA circuit (EDC) with Cas9 trans-cleavage and G-quadruplex-based electrochemical signal generation. Recognition of AFB1 or Pb2+ by the corresponding functional nucleic acids initiates the EDC and generates Cas9 activators. The activated Cas9 subsequently cleaves G-quadruplex-containing hairpin probes immobilized on the electrode surface, allowing the released G-quadruplex sequences to bind hemin and generate an enhanced electrochemical response. The combination of EDC amplification and Cas9 trans-cleavage provides dual signal amplification, achieving detection limits of 0.1 pg mL-1 for AFB1 and 0.5 pM for Pb2+. ECG-Cas9 also showed good selectivity toward both targets. Notably, the use of the G-quadruplex/hemin complex as the electrochemical signal reporter avoids additional electroactive labeling and simplifies probe preparation. Finally, the method was applied to the determination of AFB1 and Pb2+ in food and traditional Chinese medicine samples, with satisfactory analytical performance. These results suggest that ECG-Cas9 provides a sensitive and practical approach for contaminant analysis in complex samples.

papers.title: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis treated with the modified Bu-Shen-Jian-Pi decoction (mBSJP): Multicenter study.
papers.journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
papers.authors: Han X, Li R, Zhang H, Liu Y, Loong SK, Wei S et al.
papers.abstract:
To investigate whether the modified Bu-Shen-Jian-Pi decoction (mBSJP) is more efficacious than the hitherto used and promoted BSJP formula in the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
ALS is a fatal neurodegenerative disease with no satisfactory treatment option. Currently, there are few palliative care methods that can significantly delay the progression of the disease, and the efficacy of the herbal treatments used hitherto has also been unsatisfactory.
A total of 165 patients with ALS who met the diagnostic criteria after screening were randomly allocated into two groups, a modified Bu-Shen-Jian-Pi decoction group referred to as the mBSJP group and the placebo group. Clinical efficacy and side effects were evaluated during a 16-week observation period. Primary outcomes included Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Symptom Score in Integrative Treatment Scale (ALS-SSIT) and Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R) scores, and secondary observation parameters were 36-Item Short-Form Health Survey Questionnaire (SF-36) and forced vital capacity (FVC).
A total of 73 patients in the mBSJP group and 71 patients in the placebo group completed the trial. At the end of the 16th week of treatment, there were significant statistical differences observed between the two groups in values for both the ALS-SSIT and the ALSFRS-R scores showing that mBSJP significantly delayed progression of the disease and appearance of symptoms compared to the administration of placebo.
Treatment of ALS with mBSJP delays disease progression and is recommended as a treatment option for ALS in regions where the use of traditional Chinese medicine is regulated and approved.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture relieves neuropathic pain via modulation of the ferroptosis pathway through GPX4.
papers.journal: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
papers.authors: Wen X, Huang A, Kui W, Li Y, Gu Z, Xie L et al.
papers.abstract:
Neuropathic pain (NP) is a chronic condition with complex mechanisms and limited treatments. While electroacupuncture (EA) shows promising analgesic effects, its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether EA modulates ferroptosis to alleviate NP via glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4).
A chronic constriction injury (CCI) rat model was employed. EA was administered at ST36 and GB34 for 14 consecutive days. Pain hypersensitivity, neuronal injury, glial activation, ferroptosis-related markers, mitochondrial morphology and the effect of co-administration of Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) were assessed.
EA alleviated CCI-induced pain hypersensitivity, restoring mechanical withdrawal threshold (MWT) to 77.2% and paw withdrawal latency (PWL) to 85.4% of sham group levels (p < 0.01). Immunofluorescence analysis revealed that EA increased neuronal nuclei (NeuN)-positive cell counts by 41.5% (p < 0.001) while reducing glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule (Iba)-1 expression by 48.2% and 54.7%, respectively (p < 0.001). EA restored GPX4 expression (2.3-fold, p < 0.01), increased glutathione (GSH) levels, and reduced acyl-coenzyme A (CoA) synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), malondialdehyde (MDA) and iron accumulation. Furthermore, EA reversed mitochondrial shrinkage and cristae disruption. Immunofluorescence confirmed increased GPX4 co-localization in spinal neurons. Notably, co-administration with Fer-1 further enhanced neuroprotection and pain relief, suggesting additive effects.
These findings suggest that EA relieves NP by modulating GPX4-mediated ferroptosis, inhibiting lipid peroxidation and preserving mitochondrial integrity. The enhanced effect with EA and Fer-1 in combination further supports ferroptosis modulation as a potential mechanism underlying EA-induced analgesia.

papers.title: Early Acupuncture Following Thrombolysis in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials on Efficacy and Safety.
papers.authors: Li G, Zhou Y, He Z, Li S, Bai Q, Fan S et al.
papers.abstract:
Intravenous thrombolysis is standard for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but many patients still have poor outcomes. Acupuncture may confer additional neuroprotection, yet its safety and efficacy when initiated early post-thrombolysis remain unclear.
A systematic search of databases and registries was conducted from inception to March 31, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing thrombolysis plus acupuncture with thrombolysis plus conventional post-thrombolytic care in AIS patients within 14 days of onset. Meta-analyses were performed using mean differences (MD) or risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic; publication bias was evaluated via Egger's test. Pre-specified subgroup analyses were conducted.
Ten trials (1116 patients) were included. Adjunctive acupuncture reduced neurological deficit (NIHSS MD -2.90, 95% CI -3.62 to -2.17), improved activities of daily living (Barthel Index MD 12.07, 95% CI 8.10-16.03), and increased clinical response (RR 1.16, 95% CI 1.11-1.21; all p < 0.001). Adverse events did not differ significantly (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.25-1.08). Only one study reported symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (zero acupuncture vs. six control). Benefits were consistent across subgroups.
In AIS patients receiving thrombolysis, acupuncture initiated early following thrombolysis improves neurological and functional outcomes. In available safety data, adverse events did not differ significantly between groups; however, systematic surveillance for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage was lacking in most trials. These findings support further rigorous evaluation of early post-thrombolysis acupuncture in adequately monitored randomized trials.
PROSPERO CRD420261358943.

papers.title: Scoping Review of Acupuncture for Migraine: Current Evidence and Research Gaps.
papers.authors: Wu Y, Ji Y, Wu Y, Li W, Zhang J, Yao C et al.
papers.abstract:
Migraine is a disabling neurological disorder that significantly impairs quality of life and imposes a substantial socioeconomic burden. While acupuncture has shown clinical benefits for migraine management, the scope and methodological quality of the existing evidence remain unclear. This scoping review aimed to map the current landscape of clinical research on acupuncture for migraine, characterize the evidence base, identify research gaps, and inform future research priorities.
We systematically searched CNKI, WanFang, SinoMed, PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from inception to January 13, 2026. A total of 269 randomized controlled trials were included.
Most studies originated from China, with limited English-language publications. Migraine without aura was the most frequently investigated subtype, and the ICHD criteria were commonly applied. The most frequently used acupoints were GB20, GB8, and LR3, while the GB and TE meridians were selected most often. The most common body region combination targeted the head (caput) and neck (collum). Conventional acupuncture was the predominant technique, followed by electroacupuncture and blood-letting therapy. Outcome measures fell into four categories: objective headache parameters, assessment scales, efficacy and safety indicators, and mechanistic or adjunctive measures. Despite the breadth of studies, reporting quality was limited: only 1.49% of trials enrolled more than 300 participants and 43.12% did not report follow-up duration. Methodological limitations also included inadequate randomization reporting, insufficient blinding, and heterogeneity in core outcome definitions. These inconsistencies limit cross-study comparability and evidence synthesis.
Future research should prioritize rigorous methodology, standardized protocols, and candidate outcome domains to guide future consensus development, enhancing the validity and clinical applicability of acupuncture research for migraine.

papers.title: Efficacy, safety and mechanism of Jinfeng pill in the treatment of perimenopausal syndrome: A protocol for a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial.
papers.authors: Wu X, Zhou L, Hu J, Tian M, Liu S, Song K et al.
papers.abstract:
Perimenopausal syndrome (PMPS) refers to a series of physiological and psychological symptoms caused by the fluctuation or decline of sex hormone levels during the pre- and postmenopausal periods. With the acceleration of aging society, more and more women suffer from symptoms of PMPS. Jinfeng Pill (JFP) is a classic Chinese patent medicine for gynecological diseases, but it lacks rigorous clinical evidence for the treatment of PMPS.
This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial will be conducted across three hospitals in China. A total of 100 perimenopausal women will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive JFP or placebo for 12 weeks, followed by a 4-week post-treatment follow-up. The primary outcome is the modified Kupperman Index (KI), assessed at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 16. Secondary outcomes include the Hot Flash scale (HFs), the Menopause-Specific Quality of Life (MENQOL) questionnaire, the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD), the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), the Vaginal Health Index Score (VHIS), and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) symptom score. Mechanistic outcomes encompass serum sex hormones and estrogen metabolites, inflammatory cytokines interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), gut microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing), faecal β-glucuronidase (β-GUS) activity, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) concentrations.
This is the first multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to investigate the molecular mechanism by which JFP ameliorate PMPS by reshaping the gut microbiota structure, modulating β-GUS activity, optimizing SCFAs metabolism, suppressing inflammatory responses, and maintaining estrogen homeostasis. The results of this trial will help us to evaluate the efficacy, safety and possible mechanism of JFP in treating PMPS.
The protocol (Version 3.0, dated November 19, 2025) was approved by the Ethics Committee of Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology (approval number: TJ-IRB202512083). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants prior to enrolment. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and academic conference presentations.

papers.title: Thymidine mitigates LPS-induced acute lung injury by regulating gut microbiota and metabolism through the lung-gut axis.
papers.authors: Luo M, Zeng M, Zhang Y, Guo P, Zhang Z, Wu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Yam (Dioscorea opposita Thunb.) is a prominent traditional Chinese medicine with the core function of tonifying the lungs. Thymidine (Thy), a compound extracted from the stems and leaves of yam, has an unclear mechanism of action on acute lung injury (ALI).
An ALI model was established by tracheal infusion LPS. Pulmonary edema, lung histopathology, lung function, oxidative stress, immunity, and inflammation of mice were detected. The analysis of metabolomics, intestinal flora, and lung PPAR-γ levels was to clarify the mechanism of Thy on ALI. The co-culture of Beas-2B and Caco-2 was used to investigate the effects of Thy combined with the PPAR-γ agonist rosiglitazone and antagonist T0070907 on the levels of PPAR-γ, oxidative stress, inflammation, and metabolites in LPS-induced cell model.
Thy improved pulmonary edema and pathological damage in the lungs, reduced oxidative stress and immune inflammatory levels, and affected the balance of intestinal microbiota in ALI mice, as well as arachidonic acid metabolism, and regulated the levels of PPAR-γ. Under co-culture, Thy reduced oxidative stress levels in Beas-2B and Caco-2 and alleviated the levels of PPAR-γ, inflammatory factors, and metabolites in Beas-2B. And the effect of Thy was blocked by T0070907, and rosiglitazone promoted the role of Thy.
Thy may ameliorate intestinal dysbiosis and metabolic disorders via the lung-gut axis and regulate the levels of PPAR-γ to mitigate LPS-induced ALI.

papers.title: Acupuncture for healthy-ageing-relevant outcomes in older cancer survivors: a scoping review with implications for future research and practice.
papers.journal: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice
papers.authors: Lam CS, Li X, Wu HV, Zhu L, Chow V, Chimonas S et al.
papers.abstract:
Older cancer survivors face multidimensional challenges to healthy ageing and independence. Acupuncture has growing evidence for pain and symptom management, but its role in promoting healthy ageing remains unclear. This scoping review mapped evidence across four healthy-ageing-relevant domains, including physical function, psychological distress, cognition, and medication use, and identified knowledge gaps.
We searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through June 30, 2026. Eligible studies evaluated acupuncture among adult cancer survivors; studies restricted to younger populations were excluded. Findings were extracted and narratively synthesized across the four domains.
Of 986 records identified, 39 articles representing 37 studies were included. Most were randomized controlled trials (n = 21, 56.8%), and breast cancer was the most frequently studied (n = 22, 59.5%). Most studies assessed healthy-ageing-relevant outcomes as secondary outcomes in symptom-focused studies, with pain being the most common primary outcome (n = 9, 24.3%). No study specifically targeted older cancer survivors (age 65 or older). Physical function (n = 28, 75.7%) and psychological distress (n = 17, 45.9%) were the most frequently studied domains, whereas cognition (n = 8, 21.6%) and medication use (n = 10, 27.0%) were less frequently evaluated. Acupuncture showed promising improvements in functional outcomes and anxiety/depression compared with usual care or waitlist, whereas findings were more mixed with sham or active comparators and other outcomes.
Acupuncture is promising to support healthy ageing related outcomes among cancer survivors; however, rigorous controlled clinical trials focusing on older adults are lacking. Future prospective trials focusing on addressing these important and novel outcomes will inform evidence-based integration of acupuncture for older adults impacted by cancer.
Acupuncture may complement survivorship care to support healthy ageing, particularly by addressing functional limitations and psychological distress.

papers.title: Signal-amplified fluorescent biosensing for exosomes analysis and exosomes-driven high-throughput screening of traditional Chinese medicine.
papers.authors: Zhang Q, Huang F, Duan H, Liu Q, Wang H, Wang W et al.
papers.abstract: Exosomes, extracellular vesicles involved in intercellular communication and disease progression, have emerged as promising therapeutic targets and drug delivery vehicles. Targeting exosomes for drug screening offers significant potential in developing treatments for cancer. However, conventional methods for exosome-based drug discovery often lack sensitivity, specificity. To address these limitations, we propose a signal-amplified fluorescent biosensing (SAFB) system designed to screen drugs by specifically targeting exosomal biomarkers. This sensor integrates exosome-specific surface markers (Epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM)) with dual fluorescence amplification cascade probes (catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA), CdTe quantum dots (QDs)), enabling highly sensitive, label-free detection of exosomes and exosome-drug interactions. Moreover, SAFB is employed for high-throughput screening (HTS) to identify active compounds from Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). HFB-5D is screened out by inhibiting the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway to inhibit breast cancer growth. Overall, this work provides a versatile and promising tool for exosomes analysis and advancing exosome-related drug discovery.

papers.title: The Effectiveness of Non-surgical Interventions for Managing Chronic Low Back Pain.
papers.authors: Elanchezhian K, Devaraj K, Saravanan S, Raj BKS, Ravella V
papers.abstract:
Chronic low back pain (CLBP) is a widespread condition with a substantial effect on quality of life and work capacity. Non-drug, non-surgical options - physical therapy (PT), cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), and acupuncture - appear promising, yet stronger empirical evidence is still needed to confirm their value.
This study set out to compare PT, CBT, and acupuncture against standard care for the management of CLBP.
Two hundred participants with a diagnosis of CLBP took part in a randomized controlled trial and were allocated to one of four arms - PT, CBT, acupuncture, or standard-care control. Pain intensity, functional disability, quality of life, and psychological well-being were recorded at baseline and again at 6 and 12 weeks, using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), 36-item short form survey (SF-36), and beck depression inventory (BDI), respectively; outcomes were compared using analysis of variance with post hoc testing.
All three active arms outperformed the control. Both PT and acupuncture produced marked reductions in pain (VAS) and disability (ODI) scores (P < 0.01), whereas CBT produced its largest gains in psychological well-being (BDI) (P < 0.01) alongside more modest gains in pain and disability. SF-36 scores rose across every domain in the treatment arms, with PT and acupuncture producing the strongest gains in the physical-functioning and pain domains (P < 0.01).
PT, CBT, and acupuncture each represent a viable non-surgical option for CLBP, delivering meaningful gains in pain, function, and psychological well-being. Incorporating them into routine care could support a more holistic model of CLBP management, improving outcomes while lowering dependence on drug-based treatment.

papers.title: Non Pharmacological Pain Management in Sickle Cell Disease, a Narrative Review.
papers.authors: Daudi K, Bashir J, Aja L
papers.abstract:
Pain is a major cause of morbidity, disability, and reduced quality of life among people living with sickle cell disease (SCD). Although pharmacological treatment remains essential, non pharmacological interventions may provide complementary strategies for pain coping and symptom management. However, the strength of evidence supporting individual interventions varies considerably.
This narrative review aimed to critically evaluate the evidence for non pharmacological interventions used to manage acute and chronic pain in SCD, distinguish disease-specific findings from indirect evidence, identify limitations in the literature, and discuss implications for clinical practice and resource-constrained settings.
The review examined randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, observational studies, systematic reviews, and clinical practice guidelines addressing non pharmacological pain management in SCD. The evidence covered psychological and behavioral interventions, physical and sensory approaches, technology-assisted interventions, and supportive coping practices. Original SCD-specific studies were prioritized when evaluating intervention effectiveness. Findings from other chronic pain populations were treated as contextual evidence rather than proof of effectiveness in SCD.
The evidence was most developed for selected psychological and behavioral interventions, particularly cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and biofeedback in pediatric populations. In a multicenter randomized controlled trial involving adolescents with SCD, a digital CBT intervention was associated with a greater reduction in average pain intensity and fewer pain days at six months than an education control. Pediatric systematic reviews also identified studies investigating massage, virtual reality, yoga, and biofeedback; however, the evidence was limited by intervention heterogeneity, small sample sizes, methodological limitations, and inconsistent outcome reporting. The American Society of Hematology conditionally recommended massage, yoga, transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS), virtual reality, and guided audiovisual relaxation as adjuncts for acute SCD pain, based on very-low-certainty evidence. The available evidence for TENS was insufficient to establish benefit or harm. SCD-specific evidence for acupuncture, mindfulness-based interventions, hypnosis, and spiritual interventions was insufficient to establish their comparative analgesic effectiveness.
Non pharmacological interventions may complement pharmacological treatment and support pain coping in SCD, but their effectiveness should be evaluated individually rather than assumed across intervention categories. Clinical decisions should consider patient preferences, intervention-specific evidence, clinical circumstances, safety, and local resources. Larger controlled trials and implementation studies, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa and other low- and middle-income countries, are needed.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture Combined with Surround Needling for Acute Lateral Ankle Sprain in Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Hu Q, Cai Q, Qi B, Cai J, Wang J, Liang Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Acute lateral ankle sprain (ALAS) has a high incidence in adults. Improper acute-stage intervention causes prolonged pain, swelling and impaired functional recovery. Conventional ice plus brake rest has limited rehabilitation efficacy. This study investigated the clinical efficacy and safety of electroacupuncture (EA) combined with surround needling for adult ALAS.
In this single-center randomized controlled trial, 95 patients aged 18-60 years with ALAS were 1:1:1 randomized to EA+surround needling (n=34), sham EA (n=32) or control (ice+brake rest, n=29) groups. Outcomes were the Kofoed score and musculoskeletal ultrasound, assessed at baseline and weeks 1, 2, 3 and 9. Adverse events were monitored throughout.
EA improved Kofoed scores more than control or sham EA from week 2 to week 9 (adjusted mean differences 7.8-11.4, 95% CI excluding zero). Kofoed AUC (baseline to week 9, points × week) was greater with EA (675.5, 95% CI 658.3-692.8). AUC differences were 39.51 vs control (95% CI 19.32-59.70) and 24.76 vs sham EA (95% CI 6.05-43.47). EA reduced anterior talofibular ligament thickness more than both groups and calcaneofibular ligament thickness more than control.
EA combined with surround needling was superior to sham EA and ice plus brake rest in improving ankle function assessed by the Kofoed score and reducing anterior talofibular ligament thickness, and superior to ice plus brake rest in reducing calcaneofibular ligament thickness. However, larger, longer-term trials are needed to verify these findings.

papers.title: Effect of High-Power Laser Acupuncture on Fatigue and Proprioception in Chronic Nonspecific Low Back Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Elimy DA, Elsayed SH, Alshehre YM, Ismail AMA, Alshaikh FJ, Algheryafi RA et al.
papers.abstract:
To examine the effects of adding high-power laser acupuncture (HPLA) to an exercise program on back muscular fatigability and endurance, lumbar proprioception, pain severity, and pain-related self-efficacy in chronic nonspecific low back pain (CNLBP) patients.
Sixty adults with CNLBP aged 20-40 years enrolled in this double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial with equal and random assignment to receive HPLA plus exercise therapy or sham laser plus the same exercise therapy three times weekly over a six-week period. Back muscle fatigue and lumbar proprioception were assessed by an isokinetic dynamometer; endurance by the Biering-Sørensen test; pain severity by the visual analog scale; and pain-related self-efficacy using the Arabic Pain Self-Efficacy Questionnaire. Evaluations were carried out both before and just after the six-week intervention.
Within-group analyses demonstrated significant improvements across all outcomes in each group. Between-group analyses revealed significantly greater improvements in the HPLA treatment group across all measured variables (P < 0.05). At post-intervention, the HPLA group demonstrated a greater number of repetitions to fatigue (mean difference [MD] = 7.10 repetitions; 95% CI: 3.42 to 10.78) and lower lumbar proprioceptive error (MD = -1.27°; 95% CI: -1.60 to -0.93) compared with the sham group.
In cases of CNLBP, adding HPLA as an adjunct to exercise therapy may improve back muscle fatigue, endurance, lumbar proprioception, pain severity, and pain self-efficacy over a six-week intervention period. However, these short-term improvements require confirmation through longitudinal follow-up studies. Future research should emphasise dose response and long-term effects.

papers.title: From single pathways to holistic networks: unraveling the multimechanistic actions of acupuncture in depression.
papers.authors: Quan S, Xu W, Du H, Xu Z, Zhao T, Zhao M et al.
papers.abstract: Depression is a globally prevalent mental disorder; however, current pharmacological treatments are limited by a delayed onset of action and significant adverse effects. As a safe and effective non-pharmacological therapy, acupuncture demonstrates unique advantages in treating mild to moderate depression. Its antidepressant mechanisms are multifaceted. Primarily, acupuncture mitigates neuroinflammation by inhibiting classical signaling pathways (e.g., nuclear factor kappa B/NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3), modulating microglial polarization, and restoring cytokine homeostasis. Furthermore, it enhances neuroplasticity by upregulating brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression, improving synaptic plasticity, and promoting adult neurogenesis. At the cellular level, acupuncture exerts neuroprotective effects by suppressing apoptotic cascades associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and endoplasmic reticulum stress, regulating autophagic balance, and restoring neuronal excitability. Systemically, it ameliorates metabolic dysregulation by optimizing cerebral energy metabolism, modulating gut microbiota composition, and reinforcing intestinal barrier integrity. Additionally, acupuncture effectively alleviates comorbid pain by modulating peripheral nociceptive signaling and central pain-emotion feedback loops. These synergistic effects across multiple systems and targets may together ameliorate the pathophysiological alterations associated with depression. Despite these advances, current research faces challenges, including the translational gap between animal models and clinical pathology, as well as an insufficient investigation of multi-mechanism interactions. Future efforts should focus on developing clinically relevant models, integrating multi-omics technologies, conducting high-quality clinical trials, and exploring biomarker-guided personalized treatments to advance the scientific and standardized application of acupuncture for depression.

papers.title: UWMT-net: An uncertainty-weighted multi-task network for ultrasound-based three-class classification of thyroid nodules.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.authors: Li Q, Mao Z, He Y, Wang J, Yang Z
papers.abstract:
Risk stratification of thyroid nodules on ultrasound remains inconsistent in routine practice, particularly for borderline presentations. Many deep-learning studies report discrimination alone, while probability reliability and threshold-based clinical utility receive less attention.
We retrospectively included 364 development patients, each contributing one thyroid nodule labeled using surgical histopathology or fine-needle aspiration cytology. The primary analysis used a patient-level fixed training/validation/test framework, and robustness was additionally assessed with stratified patient-level five-fold cross-validation. A locked model was independently evaluated in 121 patients from the Affiliated Hospital of Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (Shandong Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine), Jinan, China. The task was formulated as three-class classification: benign, indeterminate or suspicious, and malignant.
The multimodal model outperformed clinical-only and image-only baselines, with the largest gains observed on class-balanced metrics. On the held-out test set, UWMT-Net achieved an accuracy of 0.838 and a macro-AUC of 0.943. Post-hoc temperature scaling reduced ECE from 0.040 to 0.015 without changing hard-label metrics. Five-fold cross-validation yielded a macro-AUC of 0.936 ± 0.011. In the independent external cohort, the locked model achieved an accuracy of 0.810, macro-F1 of 0.804, macro-AUC of 0.921, and ECE of 0.031. The added fusion baselines and paired bootstrap analysis supported a modest, but not statistically significant, numerical advantage of uncertainty-weighted multi-task learning.
Integrating ultrasound with structured clinical information improved three-class classification and probability reliability in the development cohort, with retained performance in the independent external cohort. Larger prospective multicenter validation remains required before clinical use.

papers.title: Transforming Growth Factor Beta/Smad Signaling: A Therapeutic Target of Chinese Herbal Medicine for Kidney Disease.
papers.authors: Shao B, Xu Z, Lu H, Guo J, Biao W, Wu M et al.
papers.abstract: Transforming growth factor beta/Smad signaling has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for kidney disease. Increasing evidence suggests that Chinese herbal medicine (CHM), including single herbs, bioactive compounds, herb pairs, and multi-herb formulas, modulates this signaling network in acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, and transitions of acute kidney injury-to-chronic kidney disease and acute kidney injury-on-chronic kidney disease. Frequently studied herbs include Rheum officinale (rhubarb), Wolfiporia cocos (Fu Ling), Scutellaria baicalensis (HuangQin), Salvia miltiorrhiza (Dan Shen), Astragalus membranaceus (Huang Qi), and Coptis chinensis (Huang Lian). Experimental studies suggest that CHM interventions act at multiple regulatory levels, including Smad3 activation, Smad3/Smad7 balance, post-translational modification, and epigenetic regulation, while also interacting with oxidative stress, ferroptosis, inflammatory signaling, microRNA regulation, gut microbiota, and renal-immune cell crosstalk. Overall, CHM shows promise as a multitarget strategy against transforming growth factor beta 1/Smad-driven kidney fibrosis, but further mechanistic and multicenter clinical trials are needed.

papers.title: From tradition to evidence-based medicine: A two-decade bibliometric analysis of acupuncture efficacy, neural mechanisms, and therapeutic integration (2005-2024).
papers.authors: Peng J, Xu H, Yang J, Liang J, Lv Y, Yao X et al.
papers.abstract:
Acupuncture has gained widespread recognition as a therapeutic intervention for various conditions, yet a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of global research trends in this field remains lacking.
This study aimed to analyze the characteristics, research hotspots, and emerging frontiers of acupuncture studies worldwide from 2005 to 2024.
A systematic search was conducted in the Web of Science Core Collection, focusing on highly cited articles. Data extraction included publication year, citation counts, research themes, author affiliations, and international collaborations. Statistical and network analyses were performed using VOSviewer and SPSS.
The top 100 most-cited articles were published between 2014 and 2021. The United States was the leading contributor (51 articles), followed by China (29 articles) and Germany (23 articles). Citation counts for these articles ranged from 127 to 757. The highest number of articles was published between 2005 and 2010. The average annual citation rate showed an increasing trend, while a negative correlation was observed between total citations and annual citation counts. Klaus Linde from the Technical University of Munich was the most prolific author. The Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews contributed the most papers (8) to the top 100 list. Research hotspots included acupuncture mechanisms (30%), particularly neural pathways for pain relief, and clinical applications (58%), such as chronic pain and mental health management.
This study provides a bibliometric analysis of the 100 most-cited articles in acupuncture research, highlighting key trends, contributors, and research focuses. The findings offer valuable insights for future studies.

papers.title: Serum metabolic alterations associated with Chaihu-Longgu-Muli decoction in adolescents with insomnia: An exploratory untargeted metabolomics study.
papers.authors: Xu HY, Meng TW, Zhao R, Huo HM, Fu YJ, Wu XY et al.
papers.abstract: Adolescent insomnia is common and is frequently accompanied by anxiety and depressive symptoms. Chaihu-Longgu-Muli decoction (CLMD) is used in traditional Chinese medicine prescriptions for insomnia; however, the biological changes associated with CLMD treatment in adolescents remain poorly characterized. This exploratory study investigated clinical symptom changes and corresponding serum metabolomic alterations associated with CLMD treatment in adolescents with chronic insomnia. Adolescents with chronic insomnia received either CLMD or cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) according to the predefined treatment-allocation procedure. A healthy control group was included for baseline metabolic comparison. Sleep quality and emotional symptoms were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), and Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS). Fasting serum samples collected before and after the intervention underwent untargeted metabolomic profiling using ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with tandem mass spectrometry. Candidate differential metabolites were identified using multivariate analysis together with a variable importance in projection score > 1.0 and nominal P < .05, followed by pathway enrichment analysis. Given the exploratory nature of the study, metabolomic findings were considered hypothesis-generating. Thirty adolescents were included in each intervention group, with an additional 10 healthy controls. Both CLMD and CBT groups showed improvements in PSQI, SAS, and SDS measures after treatment (all P < .05). Untargeted metabolomic profiling identified differences between adolescents with insomnia and healthy controls. Among the exploratory candidate metabolites, sphinganine and 3-indoleacetonitrile were higher in adolescents with insomnia, whereas ethylmethylacetic acid, choline, L-lysine 1,6-lactam, (R)-2-O-sulfolactate, cis-aconitic acid, and sorbitol were lower (all P < .05). Following CLMD treatment, these metabolites shifted toward levels observed in healthy controls. Exploratory pathway analysis implicated the intestinal immune network for IgA production, sphingolipid signaling, PPAR signaling, and bile secretion. CLMD treatment was associated with improvements in insomnia-related symptoms and concurrent changes in serum metabolic profiles in adolescents with chronic insomnia. The identified metabolites and pathways represent preliminary biological signals rather than validated biomarkers or established mechanisms. Larger studies with targeted quantitative metabolomics and independent validation are needed.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Reveals Differential Mechanisms of Four TCM Formulations in Treating Insomnia via Syndrome-Compound-Metabolite Association Networks.
papers.authors: Sun P, Yan S, Li S, Zhou Y, Liu Z, Cai J et al.
papers.abstract:
Guipi Pills (GPW), Wuling Capsule (WLC), Bailemian Capsule (BLMC), and Zaoren Anshen Capsule (ZRASC) are representative traditional Chinese medicine formulations for treating insomnia based on different syndromes of Heart-Spleen Deficiency, Heart-Kidney Disharmony, Liver Qi Stagnation with Yin Deficiency, and Heart Blood Deficiency, respectively. However, their molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
To elucidate the "same disease, different treatment" mechanisms of these four formulations against sleep deprivation-induced insomnia through an integrated multi-omics and network pharmacology strategy.
Chemical constituents were characterized by UHPLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS. A meta-analysis evaluated clinical differences and syndrome consistency. Subsequently, A mouse model of sleep deprivation was established; behavioral tests and HE/Nissl staining were performed. On this basis, fecal 16S rRNA gene sequencing, serum metabolomics, and hypothalamic transcriptomics were integrated to construct a microbiota-metabolite network. Furthermore, network pharmacology and molecular docking predicted component-target interactions. Finally, key protein expression was validated by western blot.
UHPLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS identified 87, 56, 163, and 128 compounds from GPW, WLC, BLMC, and ZRASC, respectively. Meta-analysis (62 RCTs, 6,045 patients) showed WLC and BLMC reduced PSQI scores alone or in combination; ZRASC benefited only in combination, and GPW combination benefit was borderline. Syndrome-efficacy interactions were inconsistent. In mice, all formulations alleviated neuronal damage despite heterogeneous behavioral improvements. All four formulations suppressed Alistipes and commonly reversed 39 serum metabolites enriched in glutathione metabolism and pentose phosphate pathway. Each formulation showed syndrome-related metabolic regulation. Hypothalamic transcriptomics revealed commonly downregulated genes (S100a9, Gbp5, Fpr1, Tnfsf8) and distinct patterns: lipid metabolism-immune suppression (GPW), transcriptional-metabolic inhibition (WLC), prolactin signaling (BLMC), and PPAR-driven energy repair (ZRASC). In an exploratory analysis, the number of microbiota-metabolite association pairs increased from WLC (158) to GPW (393), BLMC (836), and ZRASC (1,243); this gradient is hypothesis-generating and warrants independent validation.Network pharmacology and molecular docking predicted potential formulation-specific and common inflammatory pathway targets. Finally, western blot showed all formulations downregulated iNOS and COX2; all except WLC upregulated SLC7A11, GPX4, FTH, and Bcl2 (P < 0.05).
In this study, these four formulations showed heterogeneous, syndrome-associated patterns across microbiota remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, anti-inflammation, and anti-ferroptosis, which may help generate hypotheses regarding the "same disease, different treatment" principle. The findings provide a mechanistic basis for clinical application and a methodological reference for TCM modernization.

papers.title: Heifan Sanwei Decoction accelerates mucosal healing of acetic acid-induced oral ulceration: Potential involvement of C3/C5/C5aR1 signaling and macrophage phenotypic modulation.
papers.authors: Chen Z, Xiong Z, Liu D, Shen B, He W, Tang Q et al.
papers.abstract:
Heifan Sanwei Decoction (HFSWD) is a classic topical Mongolian and Tibetan medicinal formula within the system of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). It was first documented in Tongwa Gajid, a classic work of Tibetan medicine, and has subsequently been included in the second batch of the Catalogue of Ancient Classic Formulas. HFSWD consists of Melanterite (FeSO4·7H2O), Terminalia chebula Retz. and Eriobotrya japonica (Thunb.) Lindl.. Traditionally, it is used for ulcerative disorders of the tongue, oral cavity, and gingiva. In contemporary clinical practice, HFSWD is applied to oral inflammatory conditions, particularly recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS), characterized by ulcerative and erosive mucosal lesions. However, the pharmacological mechanisms and bioactive constituents underlying its mucosal healing effects remain largely unexplored.
This study aimed to investigate the mucosal healing-promoting effects of HFSWD in a rat model of acetic acid-induced oral ulceration and to explore the underlying mechanisms and bioactive constituents.
Oral ulcers were induced in rats by acetic acid cauterization. Following topical HFSWD treatment, ulcer area and body weight were monitored over a 9-day period. Histological repair was assessed using H&E, Masson's trichrome, and immunofluorescence staining. In vitro wound healing, tube formation, and qRT-PCR assays were conducted to validate the pro-migratory and anti-inflammatory properties of HFSWD. Proteomic profiling and Western blotting were employed to explore the underlying mechanisms. Chemical component analysis, molecular docking and molecular dynamic (MD) simulations were further applied to explore candidate bioactive constituents and their potential interactions with relevant molecular targets.
HFSWD treatment markedly reduced the ulcer area and effectively accelerated the overall wound-healing process in this model. Histological analysis revealed that HFSWD attenuated the local inflammatory response, promoted epithelial regeneration and collagen deposition, and significantly upregulated CD31 and CD206 expression while downregulating CD86. In vitro, HFSWD facilitated L929 and HOMF cell migration, enhanced angiogenesis in HUVECs, and suppressed the pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 in LPS-induced RAW264.7 macrophages. Integrated proteomic and Western blot analyses further demonstrated that HFSWD markedly downregulated the elevated levels of C3, C5 and C5aR1 in vivo, whereas it reduced iNOS and C5aR1 and upregulated Arg-1 in LPS-stimulated macrophages. In silico predictions speculated chebulinic acid and chlorogenic acid as compounds with favorable theoretical binding affinities to the target proteins C3 and C5aR1, respectively.
HFSWD accelerated mucosal healing in rats with acetic acid-induced oral ulcers, accompanied by attenuated local inflammation, promoted tissue repair, and modulated macrophage-related responses. These beneficial effects may be mediated by the suppression of complement-related inflammatory signaling involving C3, C5, and C5aR1, as well as alterations in macrophage polarization-associated markers.

papers.title: Mechanism of Tongqiao Huashuan decoction regulating neuroinflammation and its effect on intestinal flora in vascular dementia rats.
papers.authors: Cai J, Jiang X, Yu S, Tang Z, Zhu S, Huang W et al.
papers.abstract: To investigate molecular changes associated with the protective effect of Tongqiao Huashuan Decoction (THD) in vascular dementia (VD), focusing on the NF‑κB‑related inflammatory response, and to observe its influence on intestinal flora. The components of THD were identified using Liquid chromatography‑quadrupole time‑of‑flight tandem mass spectrometry (LC‑Q‑TOF‑MS/MS) with electrospray ionization in positive/negative modes, a methanol‑0.1% formic acid gradient mobile phase, and a C18 column (1.7 μm, 2.1 × 100 mm). Sprague‑Dawley rats were divided into four groups: Sham, VD, VD + TCM (THD), and VD+Donepezil (donepezil hydrochloride). Spatial learning and memory were assessed using the Morris Water Maze. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analyzed the ultrastructure of hippocampal CA1 neurons. Enzyme‑linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) detected interleukin‑1β (IL‑1β), tumor necrosis factor‑α (TNF‑α), macrophage inflammatory protein‑2 (MIP‑2), and IL‑6 in the hippocampus and serum. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) and Western blotting (WB) measured the expression of sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), NF‑κB, caspase‑1, and NOD‑like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3). Fecal flora was analyzed via 16S rRNA sequencing. LC‑Q‑TOF‑MS/MS detected 998 chemical constituents in THD extract. Among them, 24 high‑signal‑intensity constituents with mass‑spectrometry response values > 100 000 were tentatively annotated based on exact‑mass and MS/MS fragmentation matching against public databases and published literature. Compared with the Sham group, VD rats exhibited longer escape latency, hippocampal neuronal damage, elevated proinflammatory factors, upregulated caspase‑1/NLRP3/NF‑κB, and downregulated SIRT1/IκBα. THD treatment reversed these VD‑induced pathological abnormalities. In addition, THD restored intestinal flora dysbiosis observed in VD model rats. THD ameliorates VD‑related cognitive dysfunction, accompanied by altered expression of SIRT1/IκBα/NF‑κB‑related proteins and reduced pro‑inflammatory cytokines. Meanwhile, THD can restore disturbed gut microbiota in VD rats. Changes in the SIRT1/IκBα/NF‑κB signaling cascade are therefore associated with THD‑mediated protective outcomes.

papers.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Multi-Method, Multi-Target Acupoint Stimulation for Preventing Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting Following Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy.
papers.authors: Xing L, Zhou Y, Wang H, Xu C, Dong X
papers.abstract:
Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) remains a common complication following laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC).
To evaluate efficacy of a Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) acupoint stimulation model in reducing PONV incidence and improving gastrointestinal recovery after LC.
In this randomized controlled trial, 160 patients undergoing LC were assigned to standard care alone or standard care plus acupoint stimulation. After excluding 2 patients converted to open surgery, 79 patients in each group were analyzed. The intervention included transcutaneous electrical stimulation at Neiguan (PC6) and press needles at Hegu (LI4) and Zusanli (ST36). The primary outcome was PONV incidence and severity within 48 hours after surgery.
Compared with the control group, the intervention group had a higher proportion of patients without PONV (69.6% vs. 25.3%, P < 0.001) and a lower overall incidence of PONV (30.38% vs. 74.68%, P < 0.001). Time to first bowel movement was also shorter in the intervention group (1.96 ± 0.71 vs. 2.27 ± 0.92 days, P = 0.021). No significant differences were observed in time to first flatus or length of hospital stay.
Multi-method, multi-target TCM acupoint stimulation reduced PONV after LC and modestly improved gastrointestinal recovery. This simple and well-tolerated approach may serve as an adjunct to multimodal PONV prevention.

papers.title: Acupoint-Propagated Sensation During Laser Acupuncture in Bell's Palsy.
papers.authors: Wu D, Sun J, Litscher G, Zheng R
papers.abstract: This study aims to report a distinct phenomenon of propagated meridian sensation elicited by non-invasive laser acupuncture in two patients with chronic Bell's palsy and to describe the associated clinical outcomes. Two patients with Bell's palsy were recruited from the outpatient department of Otorhinolaryngology at Beijing Tongren Hospital. Both patients received laser acupuncture three times per week using a Class IV laser device. Based on traditional acupuncture theory and clinical experience, a systematic approach was used to identify potential acupoints and laser parameters. Outcome measures included the House-Brackmann Facial Nerve Grading System, the Sunnybrook Facial Grading System, electromyography, electroneurography, and the blink reflex. Both patients showed clinical improvement following laser acupuncture treatment. This case report documents patient-reported sensations propagating along meridian pathways during laser acupuncture treatment for facial paralysis. Further studies are needed to investigate the relationship between these sensations and clinical outcomes and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology, Machine Learning, and Molecular Docking Analysis of Changluo Tiaogan Dinghun Decoction for Coronary Heart Disease with Anxiety.
papers.authors: Ning B, Wang K, Lv C, Kou L, Zheng Z, Jia W et al.
papers.abstract: Coronary heart disease (CHD) and anxiety disorder frequently coexist, highlighting the need to investigate their potentially shared molecular mechanisms. Conventional therapeutic approaches have limitations, while traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) offers a potential multitarget strategy. Changluo Tiaogan Dinghun decoction (CLTGDHD) was developed for qi stagnation and blood stasis. This computational study integrated network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular docking to investigate the potential compounds and molecular targets of CLTGDHD relevant to CHD with anxiety disorder. Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets GSE100927 and GSE61672 were analyzed separately to identify disease-associated genes. GSE100927 comprises peripheral-artery atherosclerosis samples and was used as a surrogate for atherosclerosis-related processes relevant to CHD, whereas GSE61672 represents an anxiety disorder cohort. The resulting candidate genes were evaluated using a machine-learning prioritization workflow, which identified protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type C (PTPRC) as the sole retained gene. Molecular docking using the AlphaFold-predicted PTPRC structure (AF-P08575-4-F1) yielded predicted binding affinities ranging from -5.985 to -6.827 kcal/mol for five selected compounds. These findings suggest potential molecular interactions relevant to the investigated disease processes but do not establish therapeutic efficacy or a CHD-specific mechanism. Because the transcriptomic datasets represent separate populations rather than a clinically defined cohort with both CHD and anxiety disorder, the findings remain exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Further validation using appropriately defined clinical datasets and experimental models is required.

papers.title: MYC in renal cell carcinoma pathogenic mechanisms and pharmacological intervention strategies.
papers.authors: Mi H, Wei G, Zou L, Jin Q
papers.abstract: As a pleiotropic master transcriptional regulator that controls an extensive, context-dependent repertoire of target genes governing cell-fate determination, the oncoprotein c-Myc has long been regarded as an "undruggable" therapeutic target. In renal cell carcinoma (RCC), aberrant c‑Myc activation serves as a critical driver of tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, rendering it a high‑priority yet therapeutically intractable target for pharmacological intervention. To systematically delineate the research landscape and translational potential of c‑Myc in RCC, this review summarizes current advances from multiple dimensions. The structural features and physiological functions of c-Myc are first introduced, after which the role of dysregulated c-Myc signaling in mediating key malignant phenotypes of RCC, including excessive proliferation, metastasis, immune escape, and therapeutic resistance, is comprehensively summarized. Subsequently, mainstream pharmacological strategies targeting MYC signaling are reviewed, with emphasis on their molecular mechanisms, therapeutic rationale, and prospects for clinical translation. Furthermore, natural bioactive compounds and traditional Chinese medicine formulas with the potential to modulate MYC signaling in RCC are systematically categorized, with emphasis on their regulatory mechanisms, including MYC transcriptional inhibition, c-Myc protein destabilization, remodeling of downstream oncogenic transcriptional networks, and translational potential. This review integrates updated pathogenic mechanisms and pharmacological advances, providing a concise theoretical basis for developing c‑Myc-targeted innovative drugs against RCC.

papers.title: Gastrodin Attenuates Neuroinflammation and Depressive-Like Phenotypes via Modulation of the PHD2-HIF-1α/Glycolysis Axis.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Wang WS, Liu JF, Jiang MM, Li BH, Zhan XK et al.
papers.abstract:
Gastrodia elata is commonly used in traditional Chinese medicine to calm the spirit, soothe the liver, and relieve depression, primarily treating central emotional disorders such as low mood and irritability caused by emotional imbalances. Our previous research has confirmed that its main active component, gastrodin, can prevent and treat Alzheimer's disease by alleviating neuroinflammation.
To explore the therapeutic effect and molecular mechanism of GAS on inflammatory depression.
A classic LPS-induced mouse model of inflammatory depression was established, and model mice were subjected to continuous intervention with gradient doses of GAS to explore dose-dependent therapeutic effects. Multiple behavioral paradigms were applied to comprehensively evaluate depressive-like behaviors, while cortical histopathological staining was performed to assess neuronal injury and brain tissue lesions. High-throughput multi-omic screening and single-cell transcriptomic profiling were further utilized to screen key functional genes, metabolic pathways, and microglial phenotypic alterations. Combined with HIF-1α pharmacological rescue experiments, the core molecular pathway mediated by GAS was systematically verified.
Behavioral and pathological detection results confirmed that GAS treatment significantly and dose-dependently relieved LPS-induced depressive-like behaviors and alleviated neuronal damage and structural lesions in the prefrontal cortex. Network pharmacology and untargeted metabolomics indicated that gastrodin modulates HIF-1α-related pathways. Single-cell analyses further highlighted the critical role of microglia, with elevated Egln1 (PHD2) transcript abundance specifically detected in surveillance microglia. Mechanistic assays further validated that GAS markedly upregulated PHD2 activity, which facilitated the ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of HIF-1α, thereby effectively reversing neuroinflammation-triggered aberrant cerebral glycolysis and potentially contributing to the restoration of brain metabolic homeostasis.
GAS alleviates inflammatory depression by modulating the PHD2-HIF-1α-glycolysis axis in a microglial subtype-dependent manner, providing a novel targeted strategy for inflammatory depression.

papers.title: ZeXieYin Formula Attenuates Trimethylamine N-Oxide-Induced Cognitive Impairment via Modulating ZBP1-Associated PANoptotic Signaling.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Chang S, Zhou S, Wu W, He Y, Wu H et al.
papers.abstract:
ZeXieYin Formula (ZXYF), a classical prescription recorded in Huangdi Neijing, has been prescribed for centuries to invigorate the spleen, drain dampness, and transform phlegm to resolve metabolic fluid stagnation and mental clouding (Maoxuan). In traditional Chinese medicine theory, the accumulation of pathological phlegm-dampness obstructing cerebral orifices (Tan Meng Shen Qiao) represents a primary etiology of cognitive decline, conceptually aligning with modern metabolic endotoxemia induced by gut-derived trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO). Although ZXYF alleviates TMAO-induced cognitive deficits, its central neuroprotective mechanisms remain poorly defined.
This study aimed to determine whether ZXYF protects against TMAO-induced hippocampal neuronal injury and cognitive impairment by suppressing Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1)-associated PANoptotic signaling.
The standardized aqueous extract of ZXYF was chemically profiled using UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-HRMS. In vivo, mice were chronically exposed to TMAO via drinking water and treated with ZXYF (3.25 or 6.5 g/kg/day). Cognitive performance was evaluated using open field, Y-maze, novel object recognition, and Morris water maze tests. Hippocampal neuronal survival and mitochondrial ultrastructure were examined by NeuN immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy. In vitro, murine hippocampal HT-22 cells were challenged with TMAO and treated with ZXYF. Cytotoxicity, apoptosis, ZBP1 expression, PANoptotic effectors, and PANoptosome assembly (ASC/CASP8/RIPK3 colocalization) were analyzed using live-cell imaging, flow cytometry, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence.
ZXYF dose-dependently ameliorated TMAO-induced deficits in spatial learning, working memory, and object recognition without altering spontaneous locomotion or anxiety-like behavior. ZXYF attenuated pyramidal neuronal loss in hippocampal CA1 and CA3 subfields and reversed mitochondrial vacuolar degeneration. In hippocampal tissues, ZXYF downregulated ZBP1 expression, pro-apoptotic caspases (CASP3/8/9), phosphorylated MLKL, active Caspase-1, and cleaved GSDMD/GSDME. In HT-22 cells, ZXYF reduced TMAO-induced cell death and apoptosis, suppressed ZBP1-dependent PANoptotic cascades, and prevented ASC/CASP8/RIPK3 aggregation and colocalization.
ZXYF mitigates TMAO-induced cognitive impairment and hippocampal neuronal injury in experimental models, effects accompanied by the preservation of mitochondrial integrity, reduced ZBP1 expression, and attenuation of PANoptosis-related molecular changes. These findings provide experimental support for the traditional application of ZXYF in dispelling phlegm-dampness to unblock the orifices of the mind (Tan Meng Shen Qiao), highlighting its potential as an ethnopharmacological multi-target formulation against metabolic neurotoxicity.

papers.title: Chaihuang Qingfu Pills attenuate severe acute pancreatitis-associated acute lung injury by restoring efferocytosis via the NF-κB/CD47 axis.
papers.authors: Xiao W, Liu Y, Xie Y, Chen F, Han X, Yan S et al.
papers.abstract:
Chaihuang Qingfu Pills (CHQF), a traditional Chinese medicine formulation derived from the classical Qingyi Decoction, have long been used in clinical practice for severe acute pancreatitis (SAP). Our previous study demonstrated that CHQF reduces SAP-associated acute lung injury (SAP-ALI) clinically and protects against it experimentally; however, the mechanisms underlying its effects in the early stage of the disease remain unclear.
To investigate the protective effects of CHQF against early SAP-ALI and to elucidate the mechanisms by which CHQF modulates efferocytosis.
An L-arginine-induced SAP mouse model and an in vitro coculture system of pancreatic acinar and alveolar epithelial cells were used. Early-stage (6 h) lung proteomics was integrated with serum pharmacochemical profiling and network pharmacology, and the findings were validated by histopathological analysis, immunofluorescence and TUNEL staining, flow cytometry, Western blotting, ChIP-qPCR, molecular docking and pharmacological intervention.
CHQF improved survival and attenuated pancreatic and lung injury in SAP mice. Early-stage proteomics revealed broad disturbances of efferocytosis-related proteins; among them, the cell-surface "don't eat me" signal CD47 was markedly upregulated in SAP lung tissue and on apoptotic alveolar epithelial cells, accompanied by impaired efferocytosis, and these alterations were reversed by CHQF. Functionally, blockade of CD47 significantly enhanced the engulfment of apoptotic cells, establishing CD47 as a negative regulator of this process. Mechanistically, CHQF inhibited IKK-β/NF-κB pathway activation and the binding of NF-κB to the CD47 promoter, thereby suppressing CD47 transcription, as confirmed by pharmacological modulation of NF-κB in vitro.
CHQF protects against early SAP-ALI by targeting the IKK-β-NF-κB-CD47 axis to restore efferocytosis. These findings support the clinical potential of this classical formulation and highlight efferocytosis as a druggable process in inflammatory lung injury.
